observations.inspection: One circular instrument is on the left, supported by a vertical pedestal and splayed base. Its face contains a near-vertical thin member, a strong diagonal indicator from lower left toward upper right, several unnumbered short ticks along the lower-left arc, and oblique fine strokes near the upper-left rim. There are no readable numbers, units, or instrument-name labels. The ticks do not establish a quantitative scale.

Two distinct curved leads join the left apparatus to the plate assembly. The upper lead rises from the top of the circular instrument, loops high, then descends toward the left plate's horizontal connector. The lower lead starts near the bottom-right of the instrument, travels rightward below the plates, and curves upward at the right support toward the right plate's horizontal connector. The lead routes are separate and do not establish a connection between the two plates.

Two narrow upright oval plate faces stand close together on the right, the left oval slightly farther left and the right oval slightly farther right. Both have distinct outlines with a narrow intervening white separation. Short horizontal attachments approach the left face from its left and the right face from its right. No dielectric slab is visibly inserted between the faces in this static drawing.

Each plate has a separate thin vertical support stem with small collar or terminal-like features near its upper part. Each stem reaches its own splayed foot/base. The plate assembly has two stands, not one shared conductive bar. Fine paired stem strokes and attachments are visible, but their drawing alone does not license extra electrical contacts.

A broad oblique slab lies in the lower-right foreground, drawn with a quadrilateral top face and fine thickness/edge strokes. It is separate from the gap between the upright plates. A rear slab edge visually overlaps the feet region in perspective; that overlap is not evidence of an electrical connection to either stand.

There is one apparatus scene with no lettered subpanels, dimensions, numerical values, plus/minus charge marks, field arrows, equations, explicit scale legend, flags, cultural inscriptions, or written answer annotations. Thin outline and tick strokes matter for identifying apparatus detail, not for inventing numerical readings or a circuit through the slab.
